notes.text: Under Ley 546 of 1999, long-term individual housing loans carry an interest rate that must stay fixed for the life of the loan unless the parties agree to cut it, and the law's reference unit, the UVR, is indexed exclusively to consumer prices, so UVR balances and instalments rise with inflation. Because contracted rates do not reset with the policy rate, Banco de la República's moves act mainly through the pricing of new loans, while high inflation raises payments on the UVR book.

notes.text: The earthquake of 10 August 2026 damaged 203,301 homes and destroyed 51,778 across 16 departments and 498 municipalities, according to the housing ministry, which has committed an initial COP 1.7 trillion for reconstruction through Fonvivienda and the Fondo Milagro and estimates COP 19.7 trillion of housing needs over four years. Replacing lost stock will absorb construction capacity and add to demand for new homes in affected regions.

notes.text: Banco de la República's existing-home price index (IPVU) is a weighted repeat-sales index in the Case-Shiller tradition, built from successive appraisals of the same dwellings supplied by major mortgage lenders. Because it relies on appraisals of mortgaged homes it moves more smoothly than other Colombian price indices and does not capture cash purchases.
